in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 18 and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! You're asking about your son Alex who is 18 and lives with you at home.

Since Alex is over 16, his eligibility for Child Benefit depends on whether he's in approved education or training. 

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (This would include things like A-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQs up to level 3, or similar qualifications)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in approved education. He's actually started an apprenticeship though.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to clarify something important about Alex's apprenticeship.

**Is Alex's apprenticeship in England, or is it in Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland?**

This matters because according to the rules, if a child starts an apprenticeship in England, Child Benefit stops.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: His apprenticeship is in Northern Ireland.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that Alex's apprenticeship is in Northern Ireland.

Just to make sure I have all the information I need to make a proper assessment:

**How many hours per week is Alex working in his apprenticeship?**

This is important because Child Benefit stops if a child who is no longer in approved education or training starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's not working 24 hours or more - it's less than that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Let me make sure I have all the details correct:

- Alex is 18 years old
- He lives with you at home
- He is not in approved education or training
- He has started an apprenticeship in Northern Ireland (not England)
- He is working less than 24 hours per week

Just one final question to complete my assessment:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits himself.

Thank you for providing all that information about Alex's situation.

## Assessment Summary

Based on the information you've provided about Alex, I'm unable to make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit. Here's why:

**Alex's Situation:**
- He's 18 years old and lives with you
- He's not in approved education or training
- He's started an apprenticeship in Northern Ireland
- He works less than 24 hours per week
- He doesn't receive any benefits in his own right

**The Issue:**

The rules I have access to clearly state that Child Benefit stops if a child:
- Starts an **apprenticeship in England** (but Alex's is in Northern Ireland)
- Starts paid work for **24 hours or more** per week when not in education/training (but Alex works less than 24 hours)

Since Alex's apprenticeship is in Northern Ireland (not England) and he's working part-time (under 24 hours), his situation falls outside the specific guidance I've been provided.

**What You Should Do:**

I recommend that you **contact the Child Benefit Office directly** to clarify whether Alex's Northern Ireland apprenticeship at under 24 hours per week affects your Child Benefit entitlement. They'll be able to give you a definitive answer based on the complete set of rules for apprenticeships outside of England.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
